notes.meaning: The court officers went to the jail to fetch the apostles, but the cells were empty. The outer doors were still securely locked and the guards were standing outside on watch, completely unaware that anyone had left. God had brought His servants out by a miracle without breaking any locks or waking the guards.

The temple captain and chief priests were thoroughly baffled by the report and did not know what to do next. They wondered how far this matter would spread and worried that events were spinning completely out of their control. People who set themselves against God often find themselves trapped in their own confusion.

A messenger suddenly arrived with shocking news: the men who had been locked in prison were standing in the temple courts, openly teaching the crowds. Instead of running away to hide, the apostles went straight to the most public place in the city to obey God. Their boldness showed that they feared God far more than any human court.

The temple captain and his officers went to get the apostles, but they were careful not to use force because they feared the crowd would stone them. The apostles went along peacefully because they respected civil order and welcomed another chance to share the good news. Even powerful leaders who have no fear of God are often restrained by the fear of ordinary people.

The guards brought the apostles in and placed them before the Sanhedrin, which was the highest Jewish ruling council. The high priest took charge and began questioning them as lawbreakers. The apostles stood calmly before the very rulers who had the power to punish them.

The high priest accused the apostles of ignoring direct orders by filling Jerusalem with their teaching. He also claimed they were trying to blame the council for the death of Jesus. The rulers had demanded Jesus' execution, but their guilty consciences now made them hate hearing about it.

Peter and the other apostles replied that their highest duty was to obey God rather than human leaders. When earthly rulers order people to disobey God's clear commands, God's word must always come first. Christians must respect human laws, but loyalty to God is absolute.

Peter reminded the council that the God of their Jewish ancestors had raised Jesus back to life. The rulers had put Him to death on a wooden cross, a method designed to bring total shame and disgrace. God completely overturned their wicked sentence by giving Jesus life again.

God lifted Jesus to the highest place of honor at His right hand as Prince and Savior, the one who rescues us from sin. In this place of power, Jesus gives repentance—a sorrow for sin that turns the heart to God—along with complete forgiveness. These gifts of new life come only through Christ.

The apostles explained that they were eyewitnesses to these facts because they saw Jesus alive after His death. The Holy Spirit also proved these truths through miracles and changed lives among those who follow Jesus. Both human witnesses and God's Spirit confirmed that the message was true.

differ.view: Calvinists teach that obeying God means trusting in Christ, and the Holy Spirit works faith in believers and confirms God's gospel to them.
Methodists teach that God gives greater measures of the Holy Spirit's gifts and power to people who faithfully obey the Spirit's promptings.

notes.meaning: When the council heard Peter's words, they were filled with burning rage, as though a saw were ripping through their hearts. Instead of repenting of their wrongdoing, they began plotting how to put the apostles to death. Rejecting the truth often drives stubborn hearts into deeper anger.

A Pharisee named Gamaliel, a respected teacher of the law, stood up and ordered that the apostles be sent outside for a moment. He had a great reputation among the people for wisdom, so the council was willing to listen to him. God often uses calm, thoughtful people to hold back the violent anger of others.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: An early church tradition recorded in Catholic history holds that Gamaliel later became a Christian and secretly stayed on the council to help the believers.

notes.meaning: Gamaliel urged his fellow leaders to stop and think carefully before deciding what to do with the prisoners. He reminded them that as men of Israel, they should be guided by reason and God's law rather than hasty temper. Rushing into harsh actions out of anger usually leads to disaster.

Gamaliel reminded the court of a rebel named Theudas who claimed to be an important leader and gathered four hundred followers. When Theudas was killed, his followers scattered, and the entire rebellion melted away on its own. False movements that depend only on human ambition quickly fall apart once their leader dies.

Next, Gamaliel brought up Judas the Galilean, who led an uprising during the Roman census and drew away many people. He was also killed, and his followers were quickly dispersed. This second example showed that political uprisings collapse naturally without the council needing to panic.

Gamaliel advised the council to take their hands off the apostles and simply leave them alone. He reasoned that if their message came merely from human scheming, it would soon collapse just like the other uprisings. There is no need to exhaust oneself fighting things that will die out on their own.

On the other hand, Gamaliel warned that if this movement came from God, the council would never be able to stop it. Worse still, by trying to crush it, they might end up fighting directly against God Himself. No human power can ever overturn the plans of the Almighty.

The council agreed not to kill the apostles, but their anger was still strong, so they had them whipped. They repeated their strict order not to speak in the name of Jesus and then released them. The rulers hoped the pain and public shame of a beating would frighten the apostles into silence.

The apostles left the council rejoicing that God considered them worthy to suffer public shame for the name of Jesus. Instead of feeling disgraced by the whip, they counted it an honor to be treated just like their Lord. Joy from God can shine brightly even through pain and humiliation.

The apostles did not slow down for a single day, teaching openly in the temple courts and privately in homes. Their constant message was the good news that Jesus is the Christ, God's promised King and Savior. Human threats could not stop them from doing the work God gave them.
